title: Aksumite stelae mark monumental burials
summary: Large carved stelae were erected at Aksum in the third and fourth centuries CE. Their architectural details and scale offer material evidence of the resources and craftsmanship of Aksumite society.

claims.text: Large carved stelae were erected at Aksum in the third and fourth centuries CE. Their architectural details and scale offer material evidence of the resources and craftsmanship of Aksumite society.
Third–fourth-century construction envelope; individual stelae have separate histories.

These monuments are useful counterparts to contemporary monumental traditions elsewhere. Their survival does not mean the entire city was a cemetery: inscriptions, trade and religious change supply other parts of its history.
